creatures.plainWords: Reads the fake passwords, keys or crypto wallet files planted in the sandbox, or dumps passwords from memory.
creatures.why: A quiet bite out of something valuable
creatures.protect: Keep passwords and wallet keys in a password manager or hardware wallet, never in plain files on your computer.

creatures.plainWords: Reads the passwords, cookies and login sessions your web browser has saved.
creatures.why: Swallows prey bigger than itself
creatures.protect: Use a separate password manager with two-factor sign-in, and clear saved sessions on shared computers.

creatures.plainWords: Gathers several of your documents and packs them into an archive ready to take away.
creatures.why: A deep filter feeder that sweeps up everything
creatures.protect: Do not open attachments or downloads you did not expect, and keep sensitive documents in encrypted storage.

creatures.plainWords: Records every key you type.
creatures.why: A see-through head with eyes always watching
creatures.protect: Use two-factor sign-in, so a typed password alone is not enough, and install programs only from sources you trust.

creatures.plainWords: Records your screen, microphone or camera.
creatures.why: Long tube eyes that record everything
creatures.protect: Deny camera, microphone and screen-recording access to apps you do not trust, and cover the camera when it is not in use.

creatures.plainWords: Replaces what you copied, for example swapping a crypto wallet address for the attacker's.
creatures.why: A quiet swap
creatures.protect: Check the full address after pasting it, especially for crypto payments, and send a small test amount first.

creatures.plainWords: A fake sign-in page captures the username and password you type into it.
creatures.why: A lure that leads you to the jaws
creatures.protect: Open sites from your bookmarks or by typing the address yourself, and check the address bar before you sign in.

creatures.plainWords: Tries to send your data to an outside computer. The attempt is blocked.
creatures.why: Thin and slippery; slides away with the catch
creatures.protect: Use a firewall that asks before programs connect to the internet, and do not run files you did not expect.

creatures.plainWords: Tries to gain administrator rights, including by installing a driver.
creatures.why: Forces its way in
creatures.protect: Use a standard account for everyday work, and approve administrator prompts only for programs you trust.

creatures.plainWords: Adds itself to start with your computer, or creates a new user account so it can return.
creatures.why: Plants itself on the seabed and stays
creatures.protect: After opening a suspicious file, review your startup programs, scheduled tasks and user accounts, and remove anything you did not add.

creatures.plainWords: Turns off security tools, clears logs, or hides its own files or processes.
creatures.why: Uses its own light to become invisible
creatures.protect: Keep your security software switched on and set to update automatically, and check that it has not been turned off.

creatures.plainWords: Sends your web traffic elsewhere by changing the hosts file, proxy or DNS settings, or by injecting content into web pages.
creatures.why: Draws traffic toward a false light
creatures.protect: Check that your proxy and DNS settings are ones you chose, and use HTTPS sites when you sign in.

creatures.plainWords: Installs browser extensions or changes your homepage or search engine.
creatures.why: Latches on and will not let go
creatures.protect: Remove browser extensions you did not install, and check your homepage and search settings after installing anything new.

creatures.plainWords: Lets someone control your computer remotely, or uses it to send traffic, scan other machines or relay connections for others.
creatures.why: One member of a coordinated colony
creatures.protect: Turn off remote-access features you do not use, and do not allow remote-control software you did not ask for.

creatures.plainWords: Hides its code inside another running program, or tricks a trusted program into loading a fake library.
creatures.why: Lives inside the host and replaces part of it
creatures.protect: Keep your programs and operating system updated, and avoid running files from publishers you do not know.

creatures.plainWords: Downloads or creates a second program, then tries to run it.
creatures.why: A huge mouth that takes in a payload
creatures.protect: Download software only from its official site, and do not run downloaded programs you did not ask for.

creatures.plainWords: Uses your processor for crypto mining or hidden ad clicks, or starts so many processes that the system grinds to a halt.
creatures.why: Its name says "drains". It is not a true squid
creatures.protect: If your computer runs hot or slow for no reason, check Task Manager or Activity Monitor for unknown programs using lots of resources.

creatures.plainWords: Tries to delete the system files your computer needs to start and run.
creatures.why: The world serpent that ends the world
creatures.protect: Keep regular backups of your system, and use a standard account for everyday work so system folders are not writable.

creatures.plainWords: Scrambles your files so you cannot open them, then leaves a ransom note or changes your wallpaper to demand payment.
creatures.why: Seizes the ship and holds it
creatures.protect: Keep backups offline or in an account the computer cannot write to, and do not open attachments from unexpected senders.

creatures.plainWords: Deletes or overwrites your files, including backups and shadow copies that let you restore them.
creatures.why: Swallows everything whole
creatures.protect: Keep backups on a separate drive or account that is not always connected, so one infected computer cannot delete them.

creatures.plainWords: Copies itself to other computers or shared folders, or mass-mails people in your contacts.
creatures.why: Cut one off and two more grow
creatures.protect: Do not open attachments from people you do not know, and limit file sharing to the devices you actually use.

creatures.plainWords: Harm that is proven but matches none of the named findings. The debrief lists the evidence instead.
creatures.why: The real deep-sea legend, seen only in glimpses
creatures.protect: Keep your software updated and back up your files, and treat unexplained changes to settings or data as a warning sign.

system.plainWords: The agent: plans each check, writes the analysis code and retries when that code fails.
system.why: Clever, uses tools, many arms at work

system.plainWords: The sandbox: a sealed environment where the file runs. It is destroyed after each run.
system.why: Closes around the creature and holds it
